name: Basemath
title: Also daughter and wife of Esau
summary: Basemath (also known as Bashemath) was a daughter of Ishmael and wife of Esau, son of Isaac. She is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis as one of Esau's Canaanite and Ishmaelite wives, and became the mother of Reuel. Her marriage represented a connection between the family lines of Esau and Ishmael.

keyEvents.title: Esau Takes Bashemath as Wife
keyEvents.description: Esau saw that his Canaanite wives displeased his father Isaac, so he took Bashemath (Basmat), the daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebajoth, as a wife.

keyEvents.title: Mother of Reuel
keyEvents.description: Bashemath bore Reuel to Esau, and through him she became an ancestress of several Edomite clans.

keyEvents.title: Reuel's Sons and Edomite Chiefs
keyEvents.description: Through her son Reuel, Bashemath became the matriarch of Nahat, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah, who became chiefs in the land of Edom.

keyEvents.title: The Genealogy of Esau in Edom
keyEvents.description: Bashemath is mentioned in the extensive genealogy of Esau's descendants who settled in the Seir mountains and founded the people of Edom.

keyEvents.title: The Connection between Esau and Ishmael
keyEvents.description: The marriage between Esau and Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, created an important family connection between two branches of Abraham's family that were both outside the covenant line through Isaac and Jacob.
